newsitem.title: ITALY: Telecom Italia to be led by domestic investors.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Italia to be led by domestic investors.

text.p: The future shareholding of Italian telecom operator Telecom Italia will be led by a hard core of domestic investors which will be set up by the end of September, newspapers said on Friday.

Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore, citing industry ministry sources, said the Treasury had decided to keep a strong Italian foothold in Telecom Italia following its planned privatisation later this year.

The paper said the Treasury, aided by merchant banks Morgan Stanley and Euromobiliare, who are advisors in the sell-off, was in the process of setting up a hard core of Italian private and institutional investors for the telecom firm.
It said foreign carriers such as U.S. firm AT&T Corp , which recently set up a global alliance with Telecom Italia, would be allowed a stake of no more than one percent.
"It seems the fears of 'colonisation' will be dispelled by the end of the summer," the paper said. "
"The control of Telecom Italia will rest firmly in Italian hands, even if its capital will be open to foreign industrial partners and institutional investors," it added.

Some Italian political parties, particuarly the Communist Refoundation party which supports the government in parliament, have protested against a large foreign presence among the phone company's future owners.

Il Sole said the core of domestic investors was likely to hold a 10 to 15 percent stake and be made up of such Italian giants as the Agnelli family holding Ifil, banking group Istituto San Paolo di Torino and other banks.
No single company or investor will be able to hold more than three percent. -- Rome newsroom 396 678 2505
